full_judgment:
3. The facts, leading to the filing of these two appeals, in brief, are that respondent No.1 as the plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 48 of 1992 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Kulaura, Moulavibazar for a decree of permanent injunction restraining the defendants from making any interference with his peaceful possession in the suit land claiming that he purchased suit plot No. 699 comprising an area of 0.53 acre from defendant Nos.2-4 by two registered deeds of sale dated 28-1-1962 and he has since been enjoying and possessing the suit land by constructing huts, digging pond and installing tubewell thereon. The suit land has been properly demarcated and separated by putting bamboo fencing on its boundaries and he has also mutated the suit land in his name, vide Mutation Case No. 524 of 1981-1982 and has since been paying rents and taxes. The defendants threatened the plaintiff to dispossess him from the suit land and hence he was con-strained to file the suit. 

 4. Defendant Nos.1-9, appellants herein, contested the suit by filing joint written statement denying all the material statements made in the plaint. Their case, in short, is that the plaintiff purchased about 0.32 acre of land from the eastern part of the suit plot No. 699 by a registered deed of sale dated 28-1-1962 and the remaining 0.23 acre of land from the western part was never sold to him. The plaintiff's registered deed No. 597 dated 28-1-1962 is a forged document and defendant Nos. 2-4 never executed such deed nor did they sell 0.23 acre of land from the western part of the suit plot No.699 to him and the plaintiff got his name mutated in respect of the suit land without any notice to them and they have been possessing the said 0.23 acre of land in ejmali by erecting kutcha but thereon. The plaintiff, therefore, did not acquire any right, title and possession over 0.23 acre of land and, as such, the suit was liable to be dismissed. 

 6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree dated 30-10-1996 passed by the appellate Court, the plaintiff, Kuti Miah moved to the High Court Division by filing a revisional application and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No.1209 of 1997. 

 7. During the pendency of the said suit, the plaintiff prayed for an order of temporary injunction and the trial Court by an order dated 27-5-1993 directed both parties to maintain status quo in respect of the possession of the suit land, but the defendants allegedly violated the order of status quo and evicted the plaintiff from the western portion of the suit land. After that, the plaintiff filed Miscellaneous Case (Violation) No.55 of 1994 against the defendants, which was allowed on 20-2-1995 and the defendants were directed to restore and deliver possession of the western part of the suit land in favour of the plaintiff within 30 days from the date of that judgment and for violating the Court's order, they were punished with a fine of Taka 1,000. 

 8. Against the order dated 20-2-1995, the defendants preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No.16 of 1995 before the learned District Judge, Moulavibazar and the plaintiff filed cross objection No. 8 of 1995. On transfer, both the appeal and cross objection were heard analogously by the then learned Subordinate Judge, Moulavibazar, who by his judgment and order dated 30-10-1996 allowed the miscellaneous appeal setting-aside the judgment and order passed by the trial Court and also sent back the violation case to the trial Court for fresh trial. 

 9. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment passed in the appeal and the cross objection arising out of violation proceeding, the plaintiff moved to the High Court Division by filing revisional application and obtained Rule in Civil Revision Nos. 1206 of 1997. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division upon hearing both the civil revision cases by his judgment and order dated 24-4-2006 made the Rules absolute. 

 15. Having considered the exhibit-1 and exhibit-1ka, the deeds of sale dated 28-1-1962, the trial Court came to a finding that those deeds of sale were more than 30 years old and that exhibit-1ka was not cancelled by any competent court and, as such, the plaintiff could prove his prima facie title to the suit land. The trial Court also found that pursuant to the exhibit-3 series, the plaintiff paid rent of the suit land and these exhibits proved possession of the plaintiff in the suit land. 

 16. Exhibit-Ga, the report of the Advocate Commissioner, submitted by Advocate Ali Ahmed, revealed that as many as ten huts were on the suit land and that a building was under construction. The trial Court took into consideration the Advocate Commissioner's report dated 4-10-1993 (exhibit-5) submitted by Advocate Salim Ahmed Chowdhury, and found that adjacent to the under construction building a fence having the height of 4 yards was erected and that the structure was about 3/4 months old. The Advocate Commissioner also found that a house measuring 65 yards long and 4½ yards breath was erected 3/4 months back. Having considered the evidence on record and exhibit-5, the trial Court came to a finding that the plaintiff had been in possession of the suit land exclusively and that during pendency of the suit, he was dispossessed from a portion thereof by the defendants: The trial Court also considered the evidence of the witnesses in extenso and came to a finding that the plaintiff was dispossessed from a portion of the suit land by the defendants during pendency of the suit in violation of the order of status quo passed by the Court. 

 18. Having considered exhibits-1 and 1(ka), the appellate Court came to a finding that on 28-1-1962, the defendant sold the suit land to the plaintiff by registered deeds of sale Nos.496 and 497. The appellate Court further found that the defendants admitted selling of 0.32 acre of the suit land to the plaintiff by exhibit-ka and that they denied selling of 0.23 acre of land by exhibit-1(ka) to the plaintiff. The appellate Court, however, came to a finding that exhibit-1(ka) was a genuine deed. When the appellate Court found that the plaintiff, in fact, purchased the suit land by exhibits-1 and 1(ka), it should have affirmed the judgment and decree of the trail Court which decreed the suit for permanent injunction. 

 27. For violating the order of status quo, the High Court Division punished the defendants to suffer civil imprisonment for 1(one) month modifying the punishment of payment of Taka 1000 and also directed to restore possession of the suit land to the plaintiff as per direction of the trial Court. 

 28. On the facts and in the circumstances of the case, we are of the view that a civil imprisonment of 4 (four) days will be proper and accordingly, the defendants are sentenced to suffer civil imprisonment for 4(four) days. In view of the findings made above, both the appeals are dismissed with the modification of sentence. The direction regarding restoration of possession by the defendants to the plaintiff is affirmed.
